about: Every silicon datum in the repo that a board-fidelity GLS must reproduce, graded per research/PROGRAM.md ('THE priority', b23e19c). grade: hard = well-established, a model that disagrees is wrong; soft = evidence to investigate; excluded = the instrument was not verified. reproducible: how the route/bitstream that produced the datum can be rebuilt today. Read by cells/gls/fid/acceptance.py.

items.title: 128 ring oscillators (ro_many_top), 32 each at 7/15/31/63 links
items.grade_reason: n=128; window-to-window reproducibility 0.052%; the readback checks itself (constants, group echo, liveness, overflow, length order) and the scatter does not cluster by slot or group (permutation p=0.73/0.66)

items.reproducible: no -- no md5, no archived .bit/.fasm/.sdf; the per-ring measured periods are NOT in the repo (only the summary above, and it is a ratio against an SDF that no longer exists). A rebuild today is a different route.

items.title: gcd_hw livelock from fasm.cc writing run-together X_ORIG_PORT pins as I0 (nextpnr-xilinx-lut-pinmap.patch)
items.grade_reason: deterministic bitstream property: the unpatched writer's output is a pure function of the routed JSON (emulated line for line by verify/fasm_audit.py --write-unpatched pinmap); board before/after on the same source and seed: 7/16 -> 16/16. Caveat recorded: bdc/emit.py:2046 attributes a 7-of-16 board result to SELECT_PAD=4 instead, so WHICH vectors fail on the August route is soft; that the corrupted bitstream fails at all is hard; ON THIS ROUTE (fusion on, today's default) the 58 sites the unpatched writer corrupts are all bd_latch odd-bit LUTs (lat.odd) whose corruption changes no vector -- measured, see lutpinmap_gcd_nofuse for the August-like netlist

oracle.unpatched: not all vectors complete; the failure is ABSENT results (livelock), not wrong ones: err=0

items.title: gcd bb10 abs going negative (the stated mechanism of the lut-pinmap livelock)
items.grade_reason: no board read-out of the abs probe (absn_sticky) is on record anywhere in the repo; the negative abs is the mechanism patches/README.md states for the livelock, first predicted by a GLS whose own LUT decode was wrong (cells/gls/README.md:66-80); and gcd_rig.v says a fix of the blamed mechanism left the board verdict bit-identical -- the cause was revised

oracle.stated: a comparator that answers wrongly makes gcd's abs skip the negation, a goes negative, while (a != 0) never terminates

items.reproducible: covered by lutpinmap_gcd as a mechanism; the abs probe needs BDC_OP_FUSION=0 (cmp probes) and no such board run is recorded

items.title: DSP48E1 AREG=1 written as AREG=2 (nextpnr-xilinx-dsp-areg.patch)
items.grade_reason: a deterministic bitstream property, but the board showed NO functional effect (result read milliseconds later: bit-identical before and after). The acceptance test is the property, not a failure: the sim built from an unpatched FASM must model AREG=2; no kernel in the repo has an AREG=1 DSP (ipow's are AREG=0), so only verify/fasm/probe.v exercises it

oracle.board: bit-identical before and after the patch

items.provenance: August (board A/B on the patch, owner's machine; no bitstream archived). Reproduced here as the PROPERTY on cells/verify/fasm/probe.v's route (seed 1, --freq 50): AREG=1/ACASCREG=1, AREG=2/ACASCREG=2 and AREG=0 DSPs
items.reproducible: emulated, as a property: acceptance.py runs dsp_latency.py on the bits of probe.v's route (patched, and fasm_audit.py --write-unpatched areg). That the unpatched bits mean AREG=2 on silicon is the patch's statement, taken by fasm2net.py's decoder as an ASSUMPTION (cells/gls/fid/README.md, DSP48E1); no board readback of it exists

items.title: gcd_bench_gen hang: the 3-bit state register sampling an async-set latch (S_WAIT_ACK 011 -> S_RTZ 110)
items.grade_reason: stochastic (metastability): caught by the 7'h16 sticky in 5 of 8 board runs, a different run index each time; the detector was validated by a forced negative control in sim (tb_gcd_bench_gen section 6); the fix (a synchroniser) held over 3000 back-to-back transactions at RUNGAP=0. Well documented, but a rate, not a deterministic outcome, and it needs a metastability model (F3)

oracle.failure: batches park in S_WAIT_RES with o_req_s=0; illegal transition 011 -> 110 recorded by the 7'h16 sticky, 5 of 8 runs

items.reproducible: no -- no archived route; the routed GLS has no AXI host model for the bench harness and resolves every flop in zero time. The structure is checked board-free by verify/cdc_bench.sh

items.title: isprime ODATA/SIG read 0x80000000: result sampled after bench_o_ack
items.grade_reason: deterministic and repeated (200/200 runs, SIG = fold(0x80000000)), cause confirmed by the fix (odata=1, derived SIG) -- but what the bus carries after the acknowledge is a property of the kernel's route, which is not archived; and in the GLS it depends on the harness, which is not simulated

oracle.failure: ODATA = 0x80000000 on every run, kernel correct (isprime(47)=1 read directly)
oracle.fixed: odata=1, sig exactly the derived fold

items.reproducible: no -- route gone; the RTL-level regression is verify/bench_window.sh
